title: Pod liveness oscillation due to CNI IP reuse — logbook
content:
Summary:

This is a working log from the on-call shift that ran into repeated pod liveness restarts across multiple node pools in us-west-2 on Nov 3–4, 2025. Symptoms were pods entering CrashLoopBackOff driven by liveness probe failures while application logs showed no app-level errors. Investigation points to CNI IP reuse and stale conntrack entries causing packets to be sent to old pod endpoints (or dropped), triggering probe timeouts and scheduling thrash.

High-level impact:
- Affected workloads: customer-facing inference APIs (medium traffic), background batch jobs (low traffic).
- Scope: ~120 pods across 8 nodes in the gpu-spot and cpu-general pools.
- Customer impact: intermittent 5xx on health-check routes, ~2–5 minute windows of elevated p95 latency for a subset of requests. No data loss observed.

Timeline (concise):
- 2025-11-03 02:14 UTC — Pager fires: increased CrashLoopBackOff rate for svc/llm-inference us-west-2.
- 02:18 UTC — On-call (Maya) connects to cluster, observes spike in kubelet events: repeated LivenessProbeFailed for many pods.
- 02:22 UTC — Noticed pattern: failures clustered on nodes with recent pod churn (scale down/up) and nodes that had been cordoned/uncordoned by autoscaler in prior 10–20 minutes.
- 02:30 UTC — Verified app logs: processes healthy, last successful probe timestamp earlier than failures.
- 02:36 UTC — Captured tcpdump on node: probe packets leave host but SYN/ACKs do not reach kube-proxy IPVS backend for the recreated pod IP.
- 02:44 UTC — Observed conntrack table entries for recycled IPs pointing to stale veth peer endpoints.
- 02:50 UTC — Temporary mitigation applied: reduced grace period for liveness to 45s and increased probe timeout to 5s for most services (patch rollout).
- 03:10 UTC — Rolled out a kube-proxy restart on a subset of impacted nodes to flush IPVS and conntrack; observed immediate reduction in liveness failures on restarted nodes.
- 03:40 UTC — Disabled service externalTrafficPolicy change experiment (it had been toggled during earlier troubleshooting).
- 04:00 UTC — Begin longer-term mitigations and notes for action items.

Observations and evidence:
- conntrack output shows high counts of entries with 'ASSURED' state for pod IPs that no longer exist. TTLs for some entries stuck near 0 but not cleared.
- kube-proxy ipvsadm showed backends for service IPs pointing to endpoints that no longer correspond to current pod UIDs.
- Node logs: kubelet event stream shows pod deletions followed by new pod creations reusing the same IPs within seconds — this is enabled by our CNI (ipam: host-local, reclaim: immediate).
- Kernel dmesg occasionally showed 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' warnings on nodes under heavy scale activity.
- We saw a correlation between autoscaler-induced rapid drain/evict cycles and the occurrence of borked conntrack/IPVS state.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Aggressive IP reuse by CNI + delayed conntrack/iptables/ipvs cleanup -> probe packets routed to stale veth/peer -> packets dropped or misrouted -> liveness timeouts.
2) conntrack table capacity hit on some older kernels when churn is high, causing asymmetric packet drops for newly assigned IPs.
3) kube-proxy race condition where endpoints are patched out-of-order during pod churn, leaving transient backends for non-existent pods.

Mitigations applied during on-call (short-term):
- Restarted kube-proxy on impacted nodes to force ipvs/backend reconciliation (immediate improvement observed).
- Flushed conntrack on a subset of nodes: sudo conntrack -F (used sparingly due to transient connection loss).
- Toggled CNI ipam reclaim timeout to delay IP reuse (rolled yellow patch to ipam config in staging first).
- Increased liveness probe timeouts/periods for the most-sensitive routes as a band-aid to reduce noisy restarts.

Why these mitigations helped:
- kube-proxy restart triggers full re-sync of service->endpoints mapping which clears stale ipvs backends.
- conntrack flush removes stale NAT mappings that were forwarding packets incorrectly.
- Delaying IP reuse reduces probability of creating exact-IP collisions during short lived churn windows.

Runbook gaps discovered:
- No standardized guidance for when to flush conntrack vs. restarting kube-proxy. On-call chose kube-proxy restart first; we need guidance that balances connection impact vs. correctness.
- No automated monitoring alert for conntrack saturation (we only alert on kernel dmesg). Need metrics around conntrack_table_utilization per node and a runbook threshold.
- CNI ipam config defaults are too aggressive for high-churn pools (spot/scale-to-zero flows).
- Liveness probe config is overly tight for services that rely on host-network path stability for short windows after pod recreation.

Action items (owner assignments):
- SRE: add per-node conntrack utilization + alert (owner: Liam O'Connor) — JIRA SRE-1321.
- SRE/Infra: Add a kube-proxy health endpoint check and an automated remediation play: if endpoint mismatch detected, perform daemonset rolling-restart of kube-proxy on subset (owner: Priya Nair).
- CNI team: introduce configurable ipam reclaim-delay for high-churn node pools + enable in staging (owner: Jorge Alvarez).
- Product: review liveness probe SLAs with owners of inference service and recommend safe defaults (owner: Maya Chen).
- DevRel/BE teams: add a small preflight check in CI to detect extremely low liveness periods for container images (owner: assigned in SRE-1324).

Follow-ups & longer-term engineering proposals:
- Proposal A: switch from immediate ip reuse to a reclaim delay per-pool and instrument pool churn heuristics so reclaim-delay is adaptive. Pros: fewer collisions; Cons: IP exhaustion risk, need capacity planning.
- Proposal B: enhance kube-proxy with a fast-path endpoint garbage collector that evicts stale backends when it detects endpoint UID mismatch. Requires upstream work and testing.
- Proposal C: use eBPF dataplane (where available) for more deterministic packet steering that tolerates conntrack staleness better. Investigate feasibility in our distro and kernel matrix.

Low-risk config changes to roll quickly:
- Increase conntrack_max for affected node types (backed by kernel tuning playbook). Test  in staging with simulated churn.
- Adjust ipam reclaim delay to 30s for gpu-spot pools and 15s for cpu-general pools, validate in canary.

Open questions (need research):
- Is there a kernel version threshold where conntrack TTL behavior changed that explains the stuck TTLs? (Kernel matrix audit requested).
- Were any other daemonset controllers (e.g., CNI agent) crashing during the churn window causing delayed cleanup? Need kubelet/crashes audit.
- Could ipvs sync ordering be fixed by adjusting kube-proxy config flags (e.g., --conntrack-max-per-core, --cleanup-conntrack)?

Notes for incident write-up (postmortem skeleton):
- Title: Transient liveness probe failures due to conntrack/IPVS state during rapid pod churn (Nov 3, 2025).
- Summary: brief description and customer impact numbers.
- Timeline: cleaned timeline with events and evidence.
- Root cause analysis: combine CNI ipam reuse behavior + conntrack/iptables/ipvs cleanup lag + potential kube-proxy races.
- Action items: list and owners + verification criteria.
- Severity/score: P2 (intermittent 5xx with mitigation, no data loss).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets used during triage:
- Check conntrack count per node: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- Flush conntrack (careful): sudo conntrack -F
- Dump ipvs backends: sudo ipvsadm -Ln --stats
- Check kube-proxy endpoint vs endpoints list: kubectl get endpoints -o yaml svc/llm-inference; compare to ipvsadm -Ln output
- tcpdump probe capture: sudo tcpdump -i any host <pod-ip> and port <probe-port> -w /tmp/probe.pcap

Scratch/notes to self: 
- Avoid blanket conntrack flush on all nodes; prefer restart of kube-proxy unless we're hitting table-full messages on >50% nodes.
- Coordinate with infra release window before bumping conntrack_max — bumping kernel sysctls can have side effects.

References/links (in addition to linked_artifacts):
- upstream kube-proxy issue about ipvs endpoint race: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/XXXX
- CNI ipam docs (internal): confluence.redwood/cni-ipam-guides

Status: this doc is a working log, next step is to convert into a formal postmortem once owners confirm root cause tracking items.

-- Maya
